# Tobit Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_013_page_001.jpg

---

**13:1** And Tobit wrote a-prayer of rejoicing and said:

Blessed [is] the-God-who-lives-forever,
and blessed [is] his-kingdom.

**13:2** For he-chastises and he-shows-mercy;
he-leads-down to-Hades and he-leads-up,
and there-is-none who-will-escape from his-hand.

**13:3** Give-thanks to-him before the-nations, O-sons-of-Israel,
for he-has-scattered-us among them.

**13:4** Declare there his-greatness;
exalt him before every living [being],
for he [is] our-Lord and he [is] our-God,
he [is] our-Father through-all the-ages.

**13:5** He-will-chastise us for our-iniquities,
and again he-will-show-mercy
and will-gather-us from all the-nations
among-whom you-have-been-scattered.

**13:6** If you-turn to-him with your-whole heart
and with your-whole soul,
to-do truth before him,
then he-will-turn to-you
and will-not-hide his-face from you.
Now see what he-has-done with-you;
give-thanks to-him with your-whole mouth;
bless the-Lord-of-righteousness
and exalt the-King-of-the-ages.
In the-land of my-captivity I-give-thanks to-him,
and I-declare his-strength and his-greatness
to a-sinful-nation.
Turn-back, O-sinners, and-do righteousness before him;
who-knows, perhaps he-will-show-favor
and he-will-have-mercy on-you.

**13:7** I-exalt my-God;
my-soul exalts the-King-of-heaven
and rejoices in his-greatness.

**13:8** Let all speak and give-thanks to-him in Jerusalem.

**13:9** O Jerusalem, the-holy-city,
he-will-chastise you for the-works of your-sons,
and again he-will-have-mercy on-the-sons of the-righteous.

**13:10** Give-thanks worthily to-the-Lord,
and bless the-King-of-the-ages,
so-that again his-tent may-be-rebuilt in-you with-joy,
and that he-may-make-glad in-you those-who-are-captive,
and may-love in-you those-who-are-miserable
through all the-generations-of the-age.

**13:11** A-bright light will-shine to-all the-ends of the-earth;
many nations will-come from-afar to-you,
and the-inhabitants of all the-ends of the-earth
to your-holy name,
bearing-in-their-hands their-gifts
for the-King-of-heaven.
Generations of generations will-offer in-you joyful-worship,
and your-name will-be-exalted forever
through-the-ages of the-age.

**13:12** Cursed [are] all who-speak a-word of harshness against-you;
cursed [are] all who-destroy you and break-down your-walls,
and all who-overthrow your-towers
and who-set-on-fire your-dwellings;
but blessed [are] forever all who-revere you.

**13:13** Go then and-rejoice over the-sons of the-righteous,
for all will-be-gathered-together
and will-bless the-Lord-of-the-ages.

**13:14** Blessed [are] those-who-love you,
and blessed [are] those-who-will-rejoice
over your-peace.
Blessed [are] all the-men
who-will-grieve over you
for all your-afflictions,
for they-will-rejoice in-you
when they-see all your-glory,
and they-will-be-glad forever.

**13:15** My-soul, bless-the-Lord the-great-King,

**13:16** for Jerusalem will-be-built with-sapphires
and with-emeralds and with-precious-stone;
your-walls and your-towers and your-battlements
with-pure gold;
and the-streets of Jerusalem
with-beryl and ruby and stone of Ophir
will-be-paved.

**13:17** And the-gates of Jerusalem with-stones of sapphire
and with-gems will-be-built,
and all her-alleys will-cry-out "Hallelujah"
and will-say "Praise the-Lord,"
as-they-celebrate in her,
the-blessed forever and ever.

**13:18** My-soul, bless-the-Lord, the-great-King.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

Chapter 13 is a liturgical psalm in the tradition of Psalms 105–106 — a blend of personal confession, communal lament, and eschatological hope. The structure follows the classical acrostic-adjacent form of Second Temple hymnody, though not a strict Hebrew acrostic in the Greek.

Key terms: *aionōn* ("ages") appears repeatedly (vv. 1, 4, 6, 10, 11, 12, 13, 18) — I preserve it uniformly as "ages" or "age" rather than "eternity" to maintain the temporal-but-unbounded sense of the Hebrew *olam* behind it.

Verse 16: The gemstone list — *sapphirois, smaragdois, lithou timiou* — maps to the New Jerusalem tradition (Rev 21:18–21, Isa 54:11–12). I render each gem literally. "Stone of Ophir" (*lithou Ophir*) is kept as a proper-noun construct.

Verse 6 is the longest verse; it contains a complex conditional (*ean...epistrephēte*) followed by a series of imperatives and first-person declarations. The word-for-word rendering preserves the structural complexity at the cost of some English smoothness.

— EMET
